sections.html:
Central Alabama is home to Chilton County, which begins just south of Shelby County and falls within the Birmingham metro. Clanton holds the courthouse and is also the largest city. Calera, mostly in Shelby County, anchors the northern edge and links the county to Birmingham. Jemison, Maplesville and Thorsby are the other incorporated places, and Isabella, Jumbo, Mountain Creek, Mulberry, Pletcher, Stanton and Verbena are unincorporated communities.

Residents numbered 43,643 in 2010 and 45,014 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 47,708, up 6.0 percent from 2020. The 2020 census listed 17,302 households and 19,438 housing units, 11.0 percent of them vacant. Three quarters of occupied homes, 76.5 percent, belong to their occupants. Rental vacancy is 8.1 percent. Rural areas hold 85.5 percent of the population.

Most sellers are families, not investors. Much of the housing dates from the building boom of the 1980s and 1990s, which means original roofs, HVAC units and water heaters are aging. Old farmhouses and outbuildings turn up often. When a barn was demolished or a room added long ago, the county's record can still describe the earlier layout. A single district, the Chilton County School District, covers every address, so school zoning will not complicate your pitch.

sections.h2: Due dates and the delinquency calendar
sections.html:
October 1 is the due date. A balance still open after December 31 is delinquent, and the calendar below takes over.

WhenWhat happens to an unpaid account
January 1Taxes are delinquent
FebruaryAccount turned over to the probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilProperty advertised for sale
MayTax sale held

Counties are not required to mail a notice, and statements from the Revenue Commissioner are a courtesy. A house left empty during a probate case can drift into this schedule with the heirs never seeing a bill. Inherited a Chilton County house? Phone the commissioner's office right away and ask which years are owed.

Did you build, improve or remove something on or before October 1? Then you or your agent must visit the Revenue Commissioner's office by December 31 and sign a fresh assessment that describes the change.

Reportable work covers new structures and additions, pools, extensive repairs, remodeling or renovation, and anything like a new fireplace, extra bath, patio, deck, carport or garage. Re-roofing, small repairs and a coat of paint are ordinary upkeep, so nothing is filed for them.

The rule works in both directions at sale time. An addition that was never reported can leave the parcel assessed too low, and a buyer's title company may notice. A barn that is long gone but still on the record means you are paying tax on a building that does not exist. Straighten out either problem before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: How to appeal and claim exemptions
sections.html:
To contest a value, put your protest in writing and send it to the county Board of Equalization. Alabama gives you 30 days from the day written notice of the value reaches you. Code of Alabama sections 40-3-20, 40-3-24 and 40-3-25 cover the procedure.

Each year the state reviews one quarter of every county under its equalization program, which can put a parcel on a four-year reassessment rotation. The state portion of the tax is waived for homeowners past 65 and for owners who are blind or permanently and totally disabled. A local official has to hear from you first, because the homestead exemption is never applied automatically. Ask the office which forms it needs and whether you must bring proof of age or disability.

If you are selling and already hold the exemption, tell the office the house is changing hands. The buyer cannot rely on yours and will have to file a claim of their own. Timing a sale near the October 1 due date also deserves thought: agree with the buyer in the contract who pays that year's bill, and let the title company prorate it so each side covers its own months of ownership.

Recording a deed triggers a state tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, rounded up for a partial block, under section 40-22-1. The state treasury keeps two-thirds and the county keeps one-third. A separate probate recording fee applies, and the deed must come with proof of the real sales price on the state's form.

Have your closing agent total all the recording costs before closing day, so the settlement statement holds no surprises.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or repairs needed
sections.html:
We look at Chilton County houses in any condition, including those with unpaid taxes or deferred repairs, and we do not ask you to fix anything first. Selling for cash avoids the lender's appraisal and the repair haggling that so often follows an inspection.

  1. Ask the Revenue Commissioner's office for the balance, listed year by year.
  2. Collect the deed and, if the house was inherited, the probate papers.
  3. Walk the property and jot down anything that differs from the tax record, such as a removed outbuilding or an added room.
  4. Go over the figures with us and decide whether an offer suits you.

Back taxes usually come out of the sale proceeds at closing. Your title company verifies the payoff figure, files the deed and pays you the balance.

sections.h2: What happens at the closing table
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, a title company or attorney takes over the paperwork. It searches the title, asks the Revenue Commissioner's office for a current payoff, contacts any mortgage holder and prepares a settlement statement that lists every deduction. Read that statement before you sign. Taxes, any mortgage balance and recording costs come off the top, and you receive the remainder.

Sellers of inherited Chilton County property should bring a few extra items: the death certificate if the deed names someone who has died, any probate order and identification for each heir who will sign. Missing one of these can stop a closing. When a house has been vacant, also bring keys, garage openers and a note on the utilities so the transfer is smooth.

Rural parcels deserve one more check. Walk the boundaries or look at a survey if you have one, and tell the title company about any shared driveway, well or easement. These details affect what the deed says and are easy to settle early. They are hard to untangle in the last days before closing, when everyone wants to finish.

sections.h2: Pricing a Chilton County house realistically
sections.html:
Buyers here compare your house with what is for sale in Clanton, Jemison and the rural stretches around them, and a farm-style lot is judged differently from a subdivision lot. Gather a few recent sales close to your address before you accept any number, ours included. Note the age of the roof, the heating and cooling equipment and the septic or well if there is one, because each can move an offer by a real amount.

If the numbers do not work for you, you can say no. We would rather you decide with the full tax picture in hand than feel rushed. Bring any questions about the delinquency calendar to the first conversation, and we will explain how it would apply to your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the county seat of Chilton County, Alabama?
faqs.a: Clanton is the county seat and the largest city. The seat moved there in 1871 after the Grantville courthouse burned.
Yes. The 2020 census counted 85.5 percent of residents as living in rural areas and 14.5 percent in urban areas.

faqs.q: When do Chilton County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent after December 31, having come due on October 1. The tax sale follows in May.

faqs.q: Do I have to report changes to my house in Chilton County?
faqs.a: Yes, for improvements or removals made on or before October 1. Visit the Revenue Commissioner's office by December 31 to sign a new assessment. Re-roofing, minor repairs and painting do not count.

faqs.q: Can you buy a Chilton County house that needs work or has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. We look at houses in any condition, and we can review the tax account together before you decide whether to accept an offer.
